answer: Each account must bind its public key to a unique human credential, verified once by independent issuers, before it can earn reputation or claim rewards. The credential stays private; a zero-knowledge proof shows only that the account is eligible, while a spent-credential registry prevents reuse. A falcon agent can still create many keys, but each needs another verified credential, so a sybil campaign costs real identities and issuer effort. Reputation then follows verified participation, letting trust ripple through the economy without treating one anchor key as proof of honesty.
